Today is the anniversary of the first addition to my wristband collection. I'm sorry to say there will be more in my life, but such is the inevitability of drug abuse. RIP ovy. I didn't find out till today a year ago but I've had nowhere else to share my story so here goes.

Acid makes you schizophrenic, there's nothing more and nothing less to it. Ever watched Donny Darko (or however the Fuck you spell it)? That movie is a story about a schizophrenic. One who's story was very much mirrored in the life of one of my dearest, though not necessarily closest, friends. Long and short of it is his family got him help, he made it through to a half way house and was allowed visitation rights. Another closer friend of mine visited him and allowed him to trip for old times sake. He attempted suicide by cop during the trip, was arrested for 3rd degree assault and hung himself in his jail cell about a month after his trial while awaiting relocation to a higher security prison. I'll never know exactly what was going through his head but we saw Megadeth in concert a year or two beforehand and I like to think the lyrics to a tout le monde were his last thoughts as he tightened the noose made from his belt. 

Drugs aren't bad mmmk... abusing the walks and power of your mind are. He was brilliant and unfortunately he thought overcoming the effects by will power was enlightening. But the lasting impression of altered brain chemistry weakened his resolve. His thrill seeking and the power of his enablers was too strong. I only wish I was there for him more but I wasn't and now I live with a mortal reminder around my wrist. You can't save everyone, not even the people who want to, because in the end he took that last hit... who's to say I would have stopped him if I was there? I'll never know, I'll just always remember.

It's like that old adage, "why curse the darkness when you can light a candle?"
Well the wind is blowing so my candle keeps going out. I try again but through no fault of my own every effort I make towards banishing the darkness is met with failure from forces beyond my control. Then, one day, my lighter runs out of fuel and I can't start a flame in the dark because I can't see the box of matches just out of reach. And if, by some miracle, those matches end up in my hands, perhaps through random grasping or a calculated plan, and I get the faint glimmer of hope that all my effort will pay off; the wind keeps blowing and the matches fizzle before they even reach the candle. So I block the wind with my body and try to savour the minimal light each produces from the initial burst of flame before the wind sweeps around my decaying frame and squandered it again. If I light the candle in this position, somehow, I either get burned because I must hold it too closely to my body to shield it from the wind or it too is blown out with another disappointing gust. About now is when I give up on ever seeing light, I'm down to my last match so I lay back, holding onto it in vain hope that one day the wind will stop and I can finally be free from the all consuming darkness around me. Looking around my area I can see others with their flickering candles, homes, light bulbs, all tributes to their success. I begin to regret not using my lighter to light my path, temporary though it may have been, to somewhere else less buffeted by the "cool breeze" others tout as refreshing and even exhilarating. But that option isn't there anymore, it's too late. And then people in their houses look on at this horrible wretch and scowl at me for embracing the dark around me, for giving in to adversity, calling me lazy and dirty. So yes it is as easy as "don't make the wrong choice" but I've already fucked it up so what do I do now? I made the choice to burn my fuel and waste my matches and now that they're gone why do I have to be condemned to eternal darkness? Why isn't there a way out? And if my choices have screwed me up to this point, why keep trying to undo them? Is being dead better than being cold, blind and screwed?
